title: South Australian Museum
scope: Standing main public building of the South Australian Museum on North Terrace, Adelaide. Includes the linked 1915 East Wing, 1890s North Wing and glazed public entrance.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum describes the 1890s North Wing, the 1915 East Wing and the separate rear Natural Science Building.
The museum identifies the North Terrace public entrance and Morgan Thomas Lane rear approach.
State heritage number 1540 records the East Wing and its 1915 opening.
The city heritage text identifies Romanesque red brick, terracotta-dressed openings, a daylight lantern and a glazed addition. Text only.
The city archaeological assessment records that the East Wing was designed to complement the Jervois Wing. Text only.

limitations: The native footprint controls the 19-point main shell. The old East Wing courtyard tower and shallow trim project into the court. Later wing joins and current roof heights are estimates.

The historic photo controls the west-facing stone elevation and roof silhouette. Stone openings on less visible sides, the rear service elevation, metalwork and glass mullion subdivisions are approximated.
The original Terrarium crop controls the site context. Local threshold and retaining-wall elevations are estimated from the surrounding terrain.
The scope is the main public building. The adjoining library, sculpture and other landscape objects are represented by their own placements when available.
